name: Amazon S3
summary: Amazon S3 is the original and most widely used cloud storage service for storing and serving files of any kind at any scale.

free_plan_covers.note: AWS's Always Free tier for S3: 5 GB storage, 20,000 GET and 2,000 PUT requests a month, per secondary sources since AWS's own page omitted the figures.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No monthly plan; S3 is pay-as-you-go. New accounts also get up to $200 in AWS credits over 6 months.

portability.note: S3's API is the reference object storage interface; most competing providers copy it for compatibility.

direct_uploads.note: Presigned URLs let a browser PUT a file straight to a bucket, without the file passing through your server.

egress_fees.note: First 100 GB/month of data transfer out is free across all AWS services combined, then about $0.09 per GB.

setup.step: Create an AWS account; there is no charge until you actually use a service.
Create an S3 bucket and an IAM user with access limited to that bucket, then generate access keys.
Install the SDK with npm install @aws-sdk/client-s3 @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner.
Set your credentials, region, and bucket name as environment variables.
Generate a presigned PUT URL on the server so the browser can upload directly to the bucket.

builder_notes: Never put long-lived AWS access keys in client code; generate presigned URLs on the server instead.
Set a strict bucket policy and CORS configuration; S3 buckets are private by default but easy to misconfigure.
Watch data transfer out costs if the app serves large files to many users; consider a CDN in front of the bucket.
